key_insight: Shell curvature couples crack opening, sliding, and tearing, so a single loading component can activate multiple fracture modes depending on crack orientation and local curvature.
engineering_relevance: Curvature-aware fracture analysis can inform damage-resistant shellular structures by accounting for geometry-driven mode coupling and possible crack closure.
method: Develop a semi-analytical framework using Reissner shallow-shell theory.
Analyze arbitrarily inclined through-thickness cracks in isotropic shells under general mechanical loading.
Compute stress intensity factors, energy release rates, and crack-lip displacements across multiple shell geometries.
evidence_signal: The reported analyses find weak coupling in ellipsoids, generally strongest coupling in hyperboloids, complex orientation-dependent responses in cylinders, and shear-induced crack closure in hyperboloidal shells.
watch_item: Applicability is bounded by shallow-shell and isotropic-material assumptions; the abstract does not report experimental validation.
paper_title: Curvature-induced fracture mode coupling in doubly curved shells
